prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on where you are in Phoenix and what you need. A few quick questions will let me give a targeted recommendation:

- What zip code or neighborhood are you in?
- What type of system do you have (central/ducted, mini‑split, heat pump, rooftop)?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling right now) or routine repair/maintenance?
- Any brand/model info or a brief description of the problem (won’t diagnose, but helps narrow who is appropriate)?

While you answer, here are immediate steps and how to pick a good contractor:

Quick troubleshooting you can do right now
- Check the thermostat settings and batteries.
- Check circuit breakers/fuses for the AC unit.
- Replace or inspect the air filter (clogged filters often reduce cooling).
- Make sure outdoor unit is not blocked by debris.
If the unit makes loud noises, leaks, or smells like burning, turn it off and call a pro.

How to choose the best HVAC company
- Licensing & insurance: Ask for the Arizona ROC number (or state license) and proof of insurance. Don’t hire an unlicensed tech.
- Certifications: NATE-certified technicians are a plus; EPA 608 certification required for refrigerant work.
- Reviews & reputation: Check Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB and local Facebook groups. Look at recent reviews for reliability and after-service.
- Written estimate & diagnostics: Get a written estimate and have them explain the failure and options (repair vs replace).
- Warranties & parts: Check labor warranties, manufacturer warranties, and guarantees on parts.
- Transparent pricing: Avoid vague “diagnostic” fees without explanation; compare at least 2–3 quotes.
- Emergency & availability: If it’s hot now, prioritize companies that offer same‑day or emergency service.
- Red flags: Very low bids, high-pressure sales, no written estimates, unwillingness to show license/insurance.

Where to look for top local companies
- Google Maps / Yelp (sort by rating and recent reviews)
- Better Business Bureau
- Angi/HomeAdvisor for screened pros
- Local neighborhood groups for personal recommendations

If you give me your zip code and the info above, I’ll list 3–5 well-rated HVAC companies in your area and note which are best for emergency repairs vs. replacements/installation.
